explanation: Count each lowercase letter in both strings using Counter, then compare the frequency maps. Matching multiplicities are sufficient because order does not matter.
timeComplexity: O(a+b) time: count a and b characters, then compare at most 26 entries.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space under the lowercase-English contract: each Counter has at most 26 keys.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For every letter, Counter records its number of occurrences. Equality of the two maps means every letter has equal multiplicity, which is exactly the anagram condition; any mismatch makes the strings non-anagrams.
walkthrough: For "cider" and "cried", each counter contains c:1,d:1,e:1,i:1,r:1. The maps match despite the different order, so return true.
edgeCases: Only lowercase English letters occur in this contract.
Different lengths cannot have equal multiplicities.
Repeated letters must have matching counts; two empty strings are anagrams.
